physDesc.physMedium: In leather half binding with marbled sides. Handwritten label pasted on front cover inscribed in foreign hand: "En Sommerdag / Idyl / for Solo, Chor og Orchester / af / J.P.E. Hartmann / Partitur." On inserted sheet the Danish text in Emil Erslev's hand. Written in brown ink. Paper: 18 staves. Paginated pp. 1-36 in Hartmann's hand. On p. 1 Hartmann has written his instructions for the copyist in purple ink: "NB. Ved Udskrivningen af dette Partitur / iagttages at Instrumenterne komme / til at staa i følgende Orden: / Fl. Ob., Cl. Fag. Corni, / Sangstemmerne Viol.1.2, Viola, Sangstemmer, / Vla. Bas. / alle Sangstemmer omsættes i G Nøglen.". At the end of the music signed and dated: "I:P:E:H: / 25/11 54."

annot.p: Hartmann's remark about the order of the instruments arise from the fact that he in 1854 still used the old-fashioned order of instruments in his scores with strings at the top; however, in 1891, when the score was used as source for the printer's copy, he had long since changed to the modern order.

physDesc.physMedium: Written in brown ink. Paper: 16 staves. Paginated 1-39. Last page blank. At the bottom of the title page stamped "Wilhelm Hansens Musik-Forlag" and "10806" added in pencil being the plate number of the printed edition of the score from 1891. On p. 6 above the first text line added in purple ink in Hartmann's hand: "Folkevise / Volkslied".
